chapter: Rhythm Club memories and playing technique
title: Dick McDonough, Carl Kress and other studio players

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: That's right. And like Dick McDonough and Carl Kress, I made so many record dates with them.
Let's talk about them a little bit.
They did some great duo records. But they were both studio players.

Studio players and then outside jazz players. Yeah they were excellent musicians. But they could also get down and play ad lib some good jazz, especially Carl Kress, McDonough too, both of them were very good, well rounded musicians.

Oh perfect. They could play good jazz. Any number of record dates I've been on, I just can't name all of them, but oh goodness, with Teddy Wilson, with Red Norvo, with Mildred Bailey, any number of dates.
How could they cut through in a live situation playing acoustic guitar?

Well then they would have a mike right up on them, you know, and then I guess the whole setup was different then, you know drums couldn't play as loud, you know, you'd have to get down, and of course the guitar always had a mike right up there on his finger board. And they could be heard. Allen Reuss was another great rhythm.
Oh yeah, he's still very active isn't he, in California. Studio work.
Does Artie Bernstein's name ring a bell to you?
Yeah, he was another good bass player. He and I made a lot of good records together.
He's on a lot of the records that Charlie Christian made with Goodman.
